This approach aims to nurture social and emotional maturity alongside academic growth, providing targeted support for students to overcome challenges and thrive.

schools.name: Intentionally Great Learning Center
schools.description: Intentionally Great Learning Center is a microschool in Conyers, Georgia, serving students from Pre-Kindergarten through third grade. The institution utilizes a faith-driven curriculum designed to build foundational skills and character values. It distinguishes itself by offering a holistic, wraparound educational approach that integrates academic support with family resources, aiming to provide purposeful learning experiences for young children within the local community.

schools.name: Kairos Academy
schools.description: Kairos Academy is a microschool located in Hanover, Indiana, serving students from kindergarten through second grade. The institution provides personalized, faith-based education designed for individualized learning and exploration. Founded on the principle of offering an alternative educational model, Kairos Academy focuses on creating a safe environment that emphasizes fun and tailored academic experiences for young learners in Southern Indiana.

schools.name: Kainos Microschool
schools.description: Kainos Microschool serves grades four through twelve in Fort Wayne, Indiana. The institution offers a personalized, faith-based curriculum designed for students who struggle in conventional academic environments. While primarily focused on grades five through twelve, the school accommodates learners seeking adaptability to meet unique educational needs. Kainos welcomes students from diverse backgrounds and faiths but does not support those with severe physical or learning challenges.

schools.name: Velos Collective
schools.description: Velos Collective operates in Taylors, South Carolina, serving students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. This microschool convenes twice weekly on Tuesdays and Thursdays, providing a flexible, à la carte curriculum focused on life skills and select academic subjects. Participants may register for individual or multiple classes to customize their educational experience. The program emphasizes holistic development and character formation for its diverse student body.

schools.name: Academic Pods of Georgia
schools.description: Academic Pods of Georgia operates in Atlanta, Georgia, serving students from kindergarten through second grade. The school distinguishes itself by providing a small-group learning environment designed to support both academic achievement and personal development. With a focus on individualized attention and hands-on experiences, the program aims to foster social-emotional growth and cultivate a lasting interest in learning among its young students within a close-knit community setting.

founder.bio: Yunice Patrick, an Atlanta Public Schools graduate and Spelman College alumna, founded Academic Pods of Georgia. Drawing on experience in private, public, and homeschooling environments, she utilizes small-group instruction to help students master foundational skills.

schools.name: Faith Preparatory School
schools.description: Faith Preparatory School serves students from PreK through 5th grade in Lake Suzy, Florida. This hybrid microschool provides part-time preschool options alongside free Voluntary Pre-Kindergarten and traditional kindergarten curricula. The institution primarily supports families residing within Charlotte, DeSoto, and Sarasota counties by offering flexible educational models tailored to early childhood development needs.

schools.name: Space of Mind
schools.description: Space of Mind operates as a microschool in Delray Beach, Florida, serving students from PreK through 12th grade. The institution distinguishes itself by prioritizing mental health and community sustainability within its educational framework. Through the Community Classroom Project, it offers workshops and classes for all ages, covering subjects such as creative arts and culinary skills to foster a collaborative learning environment focused on reducing school-related stress.

schools.name: Hazelwood Prep
schools.description: Hazelwood Prep is a microschool in Lawrenceville, Georgia, serving grades six through twelve. The institution integrates performing arts into its curriculum to foster creativity and discipline among students. Designed as an alternative for those who thrive in creative environments, the school aims to prepare learners for college and careers through structured artistic education. This approach cultivates self-directed learning and confidence, offering a distinct educational model that emphasizes the transformative power of the arts within a rigorous academic framework.

schools.name: Arkwright Microschool and Homeschool Hybrid
schools.description: Arkwright Microschool and Homeschool Hybrid serves students in grades K through 12th grade in Ellaville, Georgia. The institution offers a holistic-classical educational model designed for small group instruction within a microschool setting. This approach integrates traditional academic structures with flexible learning environments to support student development across multiple disciplines.

schools.name: Batesville Enrichment Center
schools.description: Batesville Enrichment Center serves students from kindergarten through twelfth grade in Batesville, Indiana. The institution provides homeschool enrichment classes, elective courses, camps, clubs, and tutoring services for the local community and surrounding areas. This microschool offers a variety of academic and extracurricular opportunities designed to support diverse educational needs across all grade levels within the region.

schools.name: Eastside Academic Studies
schools.description: Eastside Academic Studies in Tucker, Georgia, serves homeschooling students in grades 7-12 through a la carte microschool classes. The program offers high school-level courses taught by state-certified educators with extensive experience. Distinctive features include hands-on, lab-based science instruction and flexible class durations ranging from 1.5 to 3 hours. The curriculum meets standards recognized by the Georgia Accrediting Commission, providing academic support within a welcoming environment for diverse families.

schools.name: St. John Paul II Preparatory School
schools.description: St. John Paul II Preparatory School operates as a Catholic Classical Hybrid institution in Saint Louis County, Missouri, serving students from Pre-K through 12th grade. The school integrates families into the educational process both academically and spiritually, offering a distinct microschool environment that emphasizes collaborative learning within the community for its diverse student body.

schools.name: Keystone Education Center
schools.description: Keystone Education Center serves students in grades 3 through 8 in Vero Beach, Florida. This private microschool specializes in providing social and skills training for learners with autism, communication disorders, or related learning disabilities. The program emphasizes small-group instruction to foster life skills development while integrating community-based field trips every Friday. Its distinct approach focuses on building self-confidence and a love of learning to support student success beyond the school environment.

schools.name: Elements Academy
schools.description: Elements Academy is a microschool located in Braintree, Massachusetts, serving students from PreK through 12th grade. The institution distinguishes itself by combining small-group education with a family wellness community model. It offers both in-person and online support for parenting strategies, specifically focusing on the "Parenting Without Punishment" methodology and lifestyle frameworks known as "In Our Elements.

schools.name: Learn Beyond The Book
schools.description: Learn Beyond The Book operates as a learning and resource center for homeschool and hybrid students in Northridge, California, serving grades K through 12th grade with some Mommy & Me classes for younger children. Classes are also held in Woodland Hills and Santa Clarita. The school offers hands-on, project-based instruction in small groups of up to 12 students, supplemented by social activities and field trips to foster community engagement.

schools.name: Thrive Preparatory
schools.description: Thrive Preparatory Academy is a microschool in Conyers, Georgia, serving students in grades 3 through 12. The institution utilizes a proprietary three-step teaching process designed to help students take ownership of their learning. Additionally, the school provides support for homeschool families through in-person and online tutoring, private lessons, and summer camps. Thrive also partners with Eastside Academic Studies to offer classes in Tucker, Georgia.

schools.name: PivotED
schools.description: PivotED is a microschool in Conroe, Texas, serving students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. The institution utilizes a mixed-age environment where progression is based on mastery rather than age or speed. Curriculum blends core academics with practical life skills, including financial literacy and problem-solving. Small group sizes allow for personalized support, enabling learners to advance at their own pace while developing independence and critical thinking abilities within a structured yet flexible framework.

founder.name: Tommi
founder.bio: Tommi, founder of PivotED, holds a Bachelor’s in Psychology from Sam Houston State University and a Master’s in Education from Texas A&M University. With over 13 years of experience teaching early childhood through elementary grades, she established the school to address student needs in traditional systems.

schools.name: Inspired Learning Academy
schools.description: Inspired Learning Academy is a K–6 microschool located in Southern Gateway, Virginia, operating within the Monroe Tutoring Center. The program serves students requiring structure and individualized attention through small classes capped at ten pupils. Its distinct approach combines targeted instruction with project-based learning to foster academic growth alongside essential social-emotional skills like collaboration and problem-solving.

founder.name: Gwenette Monroe
founder.bio: Gwenette Monroe, M.Ed., founder of Inspired Learning Academy and Monroe Tutoring Center, brings over ten years of special education expertise to serve families in Fredericksburg, Stafford, Spotsylvania, and surrounding counties.

schools.name: Alma Learning Lab
schools.description: Alma Learning Lab is a hybrid homeschool program serving Kindergarten through fifth-grade students in Williamson County, Tennessee. The school operates on a two-day onsite schedule for small-group collaborative academics, while providing home learning resources and support for the remaining days. Its distinct approach emphasizes hands-on, project-based education that integrates real-world skills, creativity, and personalized academic plans tailored to individual student strengths and interests.

founder.name: Kristi Oliva
founder.bio: Kristi Oliva founded Alma Learning Lab. A former classroom teacher, instructional designer, and program manager at Amazon, she leverages her educational background to create a learning environment focused on real-world skills and student confidence.

schools.name: Hilton Horizons Academy - Johnson City
schools.description: Hilton Horizons Academy is a hybrid microschool located in Johnson City, Tennessee, scheduled to open in Spring 2026. Serving as the institution’s second campus, it offers flexible educational options for families seeking to supplement existing homeschool programs. The curriculum includes specialized instruction in art, STEM, and gardening sustainability, providing distinct enrichment opportunities alongside core academic support for its enrolled students.

founder.name: Candice Hilton
founder.bio: Candice Hilton founded Hilton Horizons Academy in Johnson City, bringing over a decade of teaching experience. She holds a BA from Tusculum College and completed the Eastman Scholar MathElites program at East Tennessee State University.

schools.name: The House of Emet
schools.description: The House of Emet is a microschool in Tyler, Texas, serving grades 2 through 5. The program integrates biblical principles into daily instruction, emphasizing spiritual growth alongside academic development. Students receive personalized guidance in reading and math within small groups, maintaining a student-to-teacher ratio of no more than 12:1. The curriculum includes leadership training and literacy routines designed to foster clear thinking, communication skills, and emotional resilience in a faith-based environment.

founder.name: As
founder.bio: Mrs. Raj, a former classroom teacher and mother of the House of Emet, founded the microschool after her son dropped out due to being misunderstood by traditional education systems.

schools.name: Acton Academy of 30a
schools.description: Acton Academy of 30a is a microschool located in Inlet Beach, Florida, serving students from pre-kindergarten through tenth grade. The institution distinguishes itself by utilizing a learner-driven model where students set their own goals and progress at individualized paces within a collaborative environment. This approach emphasizes self-directed learning and community engagement to support academic and personal development across all grade levels.

schools.name: Acton Acres Leadership Academy
schools.description: Acton Acres Leadership Academy is a microschool located in Sadler, Texas, serving students from pre-kindergarten through twelfth grade. The institution operates as an independent educational option for families seeking alternative learning environments within the community. It provides a full continuum of academic services across all developmental stages, catering to diverse educational needs without adhering to traditional public school structures.

schools.name: Aim Academy
schools.description: Aim Academy is a microschool located in Sandy, Utah, serving students from Pre-K through sixth grade. This institution offers a small-class environment designed to provide individualized attention and flexible learning paths for its young student body. By maintaining low student-to-teacher ratios, Aim Academy focuses on creating a supportive educational setting that adapts to the specific developmental needs of children in these early academic years.

schools.name: Apollo Academy
schools.description: Apollo Academy is a microschool located in Tampa, Florida, serving students from kindergarten through sixth grade. The institution provides an intimate educational environment tailored to younger learners within this specific age range. By focusing on small class sizes and personalized attention, Apollo Academy offers a distinct alternative to traditional large-scale schooling for families seeking targeted academic support in the Tampa community.

schools.name: Evoke Academy
schools.description: Evoke Academy is a microschool located in Cedar Park, Texas, serving students from PreK through eighth grade. This institution provides a compact educational environment designed to offer personalized attention and flexible learning pathways for young learners. It operates as a specialized alternative within the local community, focusing on tailored academic support rather than traditional large-scale classroom structures.

schools.name: Inspire
schools.description: Inspire is a microschool located in Weatherford, Texas, serving students from second through sixth grade. The institution offers an educational environment tailored to the specific developmental stages of elementary and middle school children. By focusing on this narrow grade range, the school provides targeted academic support and community engagement for families seeking specialized learning options within the local area.

schools.name: Invictus
schools.description: Invictus is a microschool located in Georgetown, Texas, serving students from kindergarten through sixth grade. The institution operates as an independent educational option within the community, focusing on personalized learning environments for elementary-aged children. This school provides an alternative to traditional public schooling by offering small-group instruction tailored to individual student needs and developmental stages in the specified grade range.

schools.name: Miami Nature School
schools.description: Miami Nature School serves students from kindergarten through twelfth grade in North Miami, Florida. This microschool offers an educational environment focused on nature-based learning within Miami-Dade County. The institution provides a distinct curriculum that integrates outdoor exploration with academic instruction for its diverse student body across the specified grade levels.

schools.name: Providence of Gainesville
schools.description: Providence of Gainesville is a microschool located in Gainesville, Georgia, serving students from kindergarten through fifth grade. The institution offers an intimate educational environment designed to accommodate the specific academic and social needs of its young learners within a smaller classroom setting. This setup allows for personalized attention and tailored instructional approaches appropriate for the K-5 age group.

schools.name: Rooted
schools.description: Rooted is a microschool located in Augusta, Georgia, serving students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. The institution offers an alternative educational model tailored to diverse learning needs within the community. By focusing on personalized instruction and flexible structures, Rooted provides a distinct option for families seeking non-traditional academic environments in the Augusta area.

schools.name: Wythe Academy
schools.description: Wythe Academy is a microschool located in Atlanta, Georgia, serving students from Pre-K through 5th Grade. The institution operates on a small-scale educational model designed to provide personalized attention and flexible learning environments for young children. This approach allows for tailored instructional methods that adapt to individual student needs within a compact classroom setting.

schools.name: Nature’s Gift Microschool at Nameless Creek
schools.description: Nature’s Gift Microschool at Nameless Creek is a public charter institution serving grades K through 12 in Greenfield, Indiana. It operates as part of the Indiana Microschool Collaborative, delivering education through small-group models within local communities. Each campus accommodates between 20 and 75 students under the guidance of experienced educators who provide individualized instruction tailored to specific student needs.

schools.name: Change Makers Academy
schools.description: Change Makers Academy operates as a microschool in Nashville, Tennessee, serving students from kindergarten through fifth grade. The program facilitates small-group learning with a licensed teacher, functioning similarly to homeschooling support. The weekly schedule features core academics in the morning and hands-on enrichment activities such as STEAM, entrepreneurship, and crafting in the afternoon. Classes meet Monday through Thursday, offering flexible two- or four-day options for families seeking structured peer-based education.

founder.name: Ariel
founder.bio: Ariel founded Change Makers Academy in Nashville, Tennessee. A licensed teacher with nine years of experience, she previously taught grades 1–3 science, served as an interventionist, led a K–6 microschool, and homeschooled neurodiverse students.

schools.name: River Clermont Academy
schools.description: River Clermont Academy is a microschool located in Clermont, Florida, serving students from kindergarten through seventh grade. The institution offers an educational environment tailored to the specific developmental needs of young learners within this age range. By focusing on smaller class sizes and personalized instruction, it aims to provide a supportive academic setting for families seeking alternative schooling options in the local community.

schools.name: Practical Education and Knowledge Neurodivergent Microschool
schools.description: Practical Education and Knowledge Neurodivergent Microschool in Spring, Texas serves students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. The school maintains a six-to-one student-teacher ratio within sensory-friendly environments designed for outdoor adventure themes. Its curriculum integrates practical life skills with academics using experiential learning, short burst sessions, and regular sensory breaks. Uniquely, the institution collaborates with Applied Behavior Analysis clinics to provide on-site aides, offering flexible three-day or five-day program options tailored to individual student needs.

founder.name: P.
founder.bio: Christina Dougay founded Practical Education and Knowledge Neurodivergent Microschool, drawing on her background in education and mental health. She utilizes a trauma-informed approach to create safe, experimental learning environments for students needing alternatives to traditional public schooling.

schools.name: Endless Possibilities Academy
schools.description: Endless Possibilities Academy is a private microschool in Humble, Texas, serving grades PreK through 5th Grade. The institution emphasizes academic growth, creativity, and character development within a personalized environment. Distinctive features include small class sizes and a flexible instructional approach that utilizes hands-on learning methods to foster meaningful relationships among students and build a strong sense of community.

founder.name: Erica Peterson
founder.bio: Erica Peterson, a mother and daycare industry educator, founded Endless Possibilities Academy. She draws on professional experience and personal inspiration to provide a personalized, supportive micro-school environment for children who thrive in smaller settings with flexible learning opportunities.

schools.name: Beat Roots Academy
schools.description: Beat Roots Academy is a microschool located in Pasadena, California, serving students in grades two through three. The institution focuses on personalized and inclusive education designed to foster self-confidence, curiosity, and compassion. Its distinct approach emphasizes high expectations within a dynamic environment that encourages students to explore new ideas while connecting meaningfully with their surroundings.

founder.name: Brinda
founder.bio: Brinda founded Beat Roots Academy after advocating for her daughter Ameya’s education. She draws on pioneering models like CHIME Charter and UP Academy, alongside research by Drs. Connie Lillas and Mona Delahooke, to expand inclusive learning environments.

schools.name: Flourish Madison
schools.description: Flourish Madison is a microschool located in Nashville, Tennessee, serving students in grades six through eight. The program emphasizes developing specific skills, habits, and mindsets referred to as SuperPowers, including agency, curiosity, leadership, and persistence. Students engage in project-based learning called Pursuits designed to foster self-confidence and prepare them for navigating complex environments while cultivating the ability to learn independently.

founder.name: John
founder.bio: John co-founded Flourish Madison. An engineer and educator, he previously led Rocketship Public Schools and NetGravity. He holds degrees from Stanford and Vanderbilt University and is a Stanford DCI Fellow, Aspen Institute Crown Fellow, and Ashoka Fellow.

schools.name: Barefoot Technology Academy
schools.description: Barefoot Technology Academy serves grades 9 through 12 as a fully virtual microschool admitting students nationwide. The institution emphasizes STEM education through project-based learning and discussion-based core curriculum. Students pursue mastery of competencies by creating portfolios, completing internships, and engaging in research or volunteering to earn college credit. This model targets gifted and twice-exceptional teenagers seeking rigorous, interest-driven academic exploration beyond traditional classroom structures.

founder.name: Hi
founder.bio: Rory Foulger, Founding Director of Barefoot Technology Academy, holds degrees from Minerva University, UCL, and Falmouth University. His background spans computational science and education technology, featuring roles at Wolfram Research leading STEM programs for gifted students.

schools.name: Wonderstead
schools.description: Wonderstead is a microschool serving kindergarten through eighth-grade students in Birmingham, Alabama. The institution emphasizes a low-pressure educational environment that prioritizes individual curiosity and strong interpersonal relationships. Its daily schedule incorporates quiet study periods, hands-on projects, and outdoor activities within a naturalistic setting. This approach aims to provide a warm, structured alternative to traditional high-pressure schooling by focusing on holistic student development and intentional pacing.

founder.name: Carla Barrentine
founder.bio: Carla Barrentine founded Wonderstead, bringing thirteen years of private education and community building experience. With backgrounds in psychology, neuroscience, yoga, and postpartum care, she currently works for a local startup focused on flexible childcare.

schools.name: Little Roots Academy
schools.description: Little Roots Academy in Midlothian, Virginia, serves students in grades K through 5th Grade. The school combines virtual instruction with added structure and support for homeschool families. Faith is central to the learning experience, featuring intentional Bible instruction and values-based activities. Monthly Community Days extend learning beyond the screen into the local community, providing developmentally aligned education that honors how children grow and learn.

founder.name: Dr. Jendayi
founder.bio: Dr. Jendayi A. Stafford holds a Ph.D. in Developmental Psychology and three master’s degrees. She founded Little Roots Academy as its director, leveraging her background as a developmental psychologist, educator, certified Integrative Nutrition Health Coach, and author to lead the institution.

schools.name: Unique Minds Unite
schools.description: Unique Minds Unite is a microschool in Haiku, Hawaii, serving students in grades 6 through 8. The program focuses on early adolescents by emphasizing individuality, curiosity, and meaningful learning experiences. Classes typically consist of 11 to 14-year-olds who develop social-emotional, identity, and team-building skills. The curriculum is collaborative, with students designing their own educational paths as the school year progresses through various phases that shift daily rhythms while maintaining a consistent goal of creating an inclusive environment for all learners.

founder.name: Hi
founder.bio: Zaneta Papis founded Unique Minds Unite after twenty years in tech and raising a uniquely minded child, leveraging her background in innovation to create an afterschool program focused on creativity and problem-solving.

schools.name: Imago Dei Education Institute
schools.description: Imago Dei Education Institute serves students in grades 6–12 in Jacksonville, Florida. This homeschool-aligned program supports neurodivergent learners and those rebuilding confidence through mastery-based instruction and personalized pacing. The school provides academic coaching and executive-function support within a small, relationship-centered environment. Families maintain legal homeschooling status while partnering with the institute for consistent instruction and accountability in a Christ-centered community.

founder.name: We
founder.bio: Reginald and Abigail McNair founded Imago Dei Education Institute, leveraging their backgrounds as principals, professional development coordinators, Christian school IT administrators, and classroom educators to support twice-exceptional students.

schools.name: Roots Academy
schools.description: Roots Academy operates in Farmersville, Texas, serving students from Pre-K through fifth grade. The microschool emphasizes essential life skills and high academic standards to nurture well-rounded individuals. Its distinct approach prioritizes meeting each child at their current developmental level while fostering confidence and helping learners achieve personalized educational goals through close collaboration with families.

founder.name: My
founder.bio: Holly Jackson, a University of Texas at Austin graduate and educator since 2010, founded Roots Academy in North Texas. A homeschooling parent, she brings extensive experience in personalized learning to her new microschool venture opening next fall.

schools.name: SustainEd North Fork
schools.description: SustainEd North Fork is a microschool in Southold, New York, serving grades 9 through 12. It offers STEM-focused instruction for homeschooled students through inquiry- and project-based experiences. The curriculum emphasizes holistic sustainability, environmental studies, and real-world application. Students develop competencies in systems-thinking and collaboration while engaging in generative action within the local community.
schools.street: East River Esplanade, Stuy Town, Manhattan Community Board 6, Manhattan

founder.name: Nikki Vivion
founder.bio: Nikki Vivion founded SustainEd North Fork LLC, a STEM learning center for homeschooled students in grades 9–12 on Long Island’s North Fork. She is an experienced educator with administrative and teaching roles at independent schools, focusing on STEM, wellness, and sustainability.

schools.name: Athena Micro-Academy of Austin
schools.description: Athena Micro-Academy of Austin serves students in grades six through twelve within Austin, Texas. The school operates year-round with term breaks, offering personalized academic support and a daily Spanish immersion block named Voces. Its distinct Athena’s Council program combines direct instruction with project-based learning to develop leadership and organizational skills. Students may propose interest clubs, attend Intercession Camps, and access after-school programs or appointment-based tutoring.

founder.name: Mily
founder.bio: Mily Pérez founded Athena Micro-Academy of Austin. A Texas-born educator with a M.Ed. in Educational Leadership, she is a certified teacher and principal who previously served as Head of School at her alma mater and taught at St. Andrew's Episcopal School and The Kinkaid School.

schools.name: Atlas Learning Collective
schools.description: Atlas Learning Collective serves students in grades K through 2nd in Marion, Iowa. Founded by a licensed K–6 educator, this microschool offers flexible year-round enrollment options including two-day, three-day, and five-day schedules. The program emphasizes foundational literacy and numeracy while fostering student independence and character development. Atlas partners with families to support the academic, social, and emotional growth of its students within an intentional learning environment.

founder.bio: Atlas Learning Collective founder is a licensed K–6 educator with experience in traditional and homeschool settings.

schools.name: Calming Bee Summer Camp
schools.description: Calming Bee Summer Camp operates in Bonita, California, serving children from PreK through third grade. The program offers outdoor enrichment classes that integrate mindful practices with nature appreciation. Activities include arts, movement, games, and zoology-themed sessions featuring live animals. Classes are held outdoors in South San Diego, offering flexible scheduling options across various weeks to support social-emotional learning and creative exploration.

founder.bio: Marcela Gloriacé founded Calming Bee Summer Camp, a project originating in Medellín, Colombia, 40 years ago. With a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology and certification in Behavior Analysis, she brings over eleven years of experience teaching art and psychology to children and adults.

schools.name: Rising Scholars Early College Academy
schools.description: Rising Scholars Early College Academy serves students in grades six through twelve in Macon, Georgia. The school provides an advanced curriculum delivered through seasonal face-to-face camps located in Macon and a virtual option featuring weekly live classes, recognition meetings, and evening family gatherings. This structure allows learners to engage in supported environments tailored to their schedules while accessing rigorous academic content throughout the year.

founder.name: Dr. Farryn
founder.bio: Dr. Farryn Slaton-Barkley founded Rising Scholars Early College Academy. She holds a PhD from Clark Atlanta University, degrees from Cornell University, the Universidad de Granada, and Western New Mexico University, along with New Leaders fellowship training in transformational leadership.

schools.name: EverRoot Academy
schools.description: EverRoot Academy is a K–8 school in Crestview, Florida, offering flexible virtual learning options for students seeking accessibility beyond traditional systems. The academy provides multiple enrollment plans, including three-day, four-day, and targeted tutoring models delivered over a twelve-month instructional year. Designed to support learners who are frequently on the move, EverRoot Academy emphasizes critical inquiry, community, and empowerment while creating consistent learning experiences accessible from anywhere.

founder.name: Katelynn Stone
founder.bio: Katelynn Stone founded EverRoot Academy. With 18 years of experience as an educator and administrator, she holds a Master’s in Educational Leadership, K–12 administrative certification, and 6–12 ELA certification with an ESL endorsement.

schools.name: Yes I Can Preparatory Center
schools.description: Yes I Can Preparatory Center is a faith-based microschool in Northport, Alabama, serving students from kindergarten through eighth grade. The institution supports nontraditional learners and homeschoolers by blending academic instruction with character building and leadership development. Daily routines incorporate music, movement, and creative exploration to address both academic needs and behavioral guidance within a flexible enrollment framework designed for holistic student growth.

founder.name: Hi
founder.bio: Geraldyne, founder of Yes I Can Preparatory Center and director of The Care House, draws on a family of educators and over 20 years of teaching experience to establish an academic and behavioral support microschool.

schools.name: Magnolia Concepts
schools.description: Magnolia Concepts operates as a project-based microschool in Knoxville, Tennessee, serving students from PreK through third grade. Beginning in September 2026, the institution utilizes small, mixed-age learning communities to facilitate hands-on academic instruction alongside creative exploration and outdoor activities. This approach blends homeschooling flexibility with structured guidance, emphasizing the development of empathy and collaboration while allowing children to pursue individual interests at their own pace within a supportive environment.

founder.name: Rachael
founder.bio: Rachael founded Magnolia Concepts, drawing on her experience guiding her child’s individualized, research-based education. Her background informs the school’s focus on flexible, small-group learning and personalized instruction.

schools.name: Brighter Futures Microschool
schools.description: Brighter Futures Microschool in Arlington, Texas, serves students in grades 1 through 6 with learning, language, or social differences requiring individualized instruction. The school utilizes small, skill-based groups of three to five students. Trained teachers deliver explicit, systematic, and evidence-based education across all subjects, allowing each child to work at their appropriate academic level while developing confidence and real-world skills within a focused environment.

founder.name: Brittany Lopez
founder.bio: Brittany Lopez holds degrees in Early Childhood, Elementary, and Special Education. A certified special education teacher and Professional Educational Therapist, she founded Brighter Futures Microschool after over a decade of experience supporting diverse learning needs across various instructional settings.

schools.name: Academy of Business & Innovation
schools.description: Academy of Business & Innovation is a fully virtual private high school in McKinney, Texas, serving grades 9 through 12. It offers a mastery-based curriculum aligned with CLEP standards, allowing students to earn up to 60 college credits. The program blends weekly live instruction with collaborative labs and discussion-based seminars led by business mentors. Graduates receive a professional portfolio alongside their transcript, focusing on real-world decision-making skills and peer cohort collaboration.

founder.name: The
founder.bio: The founder of Academy of Business & Innovation is a university educator with experience teaching at the University of Texas at Dallas, University of Texas at Arlington, University of North Texas, Duquesne University, and Collin College.

schools.name: Amma Mountain Academy
schools.description: Amma Mountain Academy is a hybrid microschool in Gatlinburg, Tennessee, serving grades K through 8. The institution utilizes a split-day model featuring morning academics and afternoon project-based enrichment. Students engage with local artisans and receive structured support for homeschooling families through both group and individualized instruction. The program emphasizes holistic development by integrating social-emotional learning with academic goals, offering flexible part-time or full-time enrollment options to accommodate diverse scheduling needs.

founder.name: Amanda Mc
founder.bio: Amanda McKay founded Amma Mountain Academy in Gatlinburg, Tennessee. A certified educator with over a decade of experience, she holds a BA in Interdisciplinary Studies K-8 and an MA in Secondary Education with a 6-12 English Language Arts endorsement.

schools.name: J&D Global Academy
schools.description: J&D Global Academy in West Palm Beach, Florida, serves students in kindergarten through eighth grade. The institution emphasizes global competencies alongside standard academic instruction by integrating thematic, interdisciplinary, and inquiry-driven methodologies. Each grade level incorporates project-based learning with specific global themes woven into the curriculum. This approach aims to prepare learners for future challenges while maintaining a focus on real-world relevance and ethical development within a diverse student body.

founder.name: Dr. Laura
founder.bio: Dr. Laura Jones founded J&D Global Academy. With over 20 years of instructional experience, she holds a doctorate in Global Leadership, a master’s in Human Resource Development and Administration, a bachelor’s in Business Administration, an Instructional Design certification, and Florida teaching licensure.

schools.name: Mosaic Academy
schools.description: Located in Conway, Arkansas, Mosaic Academy serves students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. Founded by educator Lori Cole, the institution utilizes a personalized educational model that prioritizes individual strengths and distinct learning profiles over standardized curricula. The school provides tailored academic support designed to build student confidence and accommodate diverse educational needs within its K-12 framework.

founder.name: As
founder.bio: Lori Cole founded Mosaic Academy, leveraging over 26 years of experience in general and special education. Her background working with diverse learning profiles informs the school’s commitment to intentional, individualized instruction.

schools.name: InnerQuest Academy
schools.description: InnerQuest Academy is a microschool located in Flossmoor, Illinois, serving students in grades eight through twelve. The institution focuses on preparing young people for the emerging AI economy by cultivating self-discovery, identity development, wellness, creativity, entrepreneurship, and technological aptitude. Through group coaching, real-world projects, micro-ventures, and collaborative innovation, the school aims to develop the mindset and skills necessary for students to build meaningful careers and contribute to societal progress.

founder.name: Barry Sean
founder.bio: Barry Sean Riley, MDIV, co-founded InnerQuest Academy. He holds degrees from Garrett Evangelical Theological Seminary and Howard University, with over two decades of experience designing educational programs in Chicago high schools and grammar schools.

schools.name: Rays of Hidden Light Academy
schools.description: Rays of Hidden Light Academy is a hybrid microschool in Douglasville, Georgia, serving grades six through twelve. Its distinct Creative Pods program allows students to explore diverse interests including art, podcasting, filmmaking, pottery, writing, music, coding, and clothing design. This approach aims to help students develop real-world skills while receiving personalized academic support in a smaller educational setting.

founder.name: With
founder.bio: Latoya Moore founded Rays of Hidden Light Academy, drawing on nearly two decades of experience as a classroom educator and academic coach to support diverse learners and improve instructional outcomes.

schools.name: Fireside Academy

Daily activities emphasize connection with nature and community through gardening, animal care, and environmental stewardship, focusing on holistic development within a microschool setting.

founder.bio: of Fireside Academy, she draws on experience as a Montessori teacher and full-time nanny. Her background includes personal reflection on twelve years in traditional education, shaping her approach to creating a learning environment focused on inner peace and self-discovery.

schools.name: Brilliant Minds Christian Academy
schools.description: Brilliant Minds Christian Academy is a private institution located in Humble, Texas, serving students from Pre-K through second grade. The school integrates Christian faith with its academic curriculum, emphasizing spiritual growth alongside character development and critical thinking. It utilizes individualized instruction to support early childhood education, aiming to build strong academic foundations while fostering moral integrity within a supportive community environment for young learners.

founder.name: With
founder.bio: Sharita Bourgeois-Clark, founder of Brilliant Minds Christian Academy, has over 16 years of education experience. Previously nominated for Teacher of the Year, she homeschooled her two children for four years each before founding her microschool.

schools.name: God's Little People Learning Academy
schools.description: God's Little People Learning Academy is a faith-based microschool in Houston, Texas, serving students from Pre-K through 2nd grade. Founded by educators with over forty years of combined experience, the school offers personalized instruction blending teacher-led lessons with inquiry-based learning. The curriculum emphasizes early literacy and whole-child development, incorporating morning prayer, sensory supports, flexible seating, and small-group sessions to foster academic and social growth within an intimate setting.

founder.name: God
founder.bio: Mar'Keda P. Gould holds a BS in Human Sciences with over ten years of teaching experience. Jacqueline Gould is a licensed childcare director with more than thirty years in early childhood education. Together, they founded God's Little People Learning Academy.

schools.name: The Pathfinder Academy
schools.description: The Pathfinder Academy is a full-time private high school in Raleigh, North Carolina, serving ninth through twelfth graders. Founded by veteran physics educator Stacey Kaufman, the institution emphasizes inquiry and project-based learning to promote critical thinking. Students engage in hands-on problem solving and authentic experiences within a collaborative community designed to foster independent thought and self-direction, preparing graduates for life beyond high school.

founder.name: Stacey Kaufman
founder.bio: Stacey Kaufman founded The Pathfinder Academy. She holds a B.S. in Physics and an M.S. in Secondary Science Education from the University of Tennessee. A veteran educator with nearly two decades of experience, she previously served as Science Department Head at Research Triangle High School.

schools.name: Forest STEAM Academy
schools.description: Forest STEAM Academy serves grades 6 through 12 in Spring Branch, Texas. Located near a river within a wooded setting, the school focuses on kinesthetic learning for middle and high school students. The curriculum emphasizes experience-based education where academic progress is assessed via portfolios and meaningful projects rather than traditional testing. This approach aims to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills through direct engagement with the natural environment.

founder.name: During
founder.bio: The founder of Forest STEAM Academy previously co-owned and managed an IT business for nearly two decades, specializing in project management. Her background includes extensive community mentorship through leading Girl Scout troops, coaching sports, directing cheer squads, and teaching art and outdoor lessons.

schools.name: The SOAR Academy
schools.description: The SOAR Academy is a microschool located in Randallstown, Maryland, serving students from kindergarten through fifth grade. The institution offers a full-time academic program that integrates core subjects with instruction in entrepreneurship, financial literacy, STEM, leadership development, and physical wellness. Founded by Andréa Harper, M.Ed., the school utilizes an intentional daily schedule to provide a structured learning environment focused on personalized student support and preparation for future leadership roles.

founder.name: Andr
founder.bio: Andréa Harper, M.Ed., founded The SOAR Academy after over a decade in public education instructional support, HR, and operations. As an educational leader and mother, she established the school to bridge strong academics with real-world preparation.

schools.name: Envision Empowerment Academy
schools.description: Envision Empowerment Academy in Petal, Mississippi, serves grades 6 through 10 as a complex-based hybrid micro-school. The program offers rigorous core academics aligned with state standards alongside optional dual enrollment opportunities for advanced credit. Students design personalized learning pathways supported by mentorship and structured accountability. A distinct feature includes entrepreneurship courses where learners develop viable businesses, reinforcing social-emotional development and leadership skills to prepare students for college readiness and real-world impact.

founder.name: Shaft V.
founder.bio: Shaft V. Brown holds a BA in Elementary Education and an MA in Adult Education and Training. With over 20 years of experience as a teacher, curriculum developer, and consultant for Mississippi agencies, he founded Envision Empowerment Academy.

schools.name: Ascension Leadership Academy
schools.description: Ascension Leadership Academy serves sixth through eighth graders in Indianapolis, Indiana. This microschool integrates STEM learning with service-based entrepreneurship and nature-based experiences. Daily routines include intentional emotional check-ins and guided reflection to support student well-being. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary projects and community engagement alongside academic rigor. Families collaborate closely with the school to foster equity and compassion within a structured, responsive educational environment focused on lifelong skill development.

founder.bio: of Ascension Leadership Academy, she leverages eight years in special education and residential treatment experience to address systemic barriers. Her background informs a strategic approach prioritizing individualized support, family partnership, and equity within the microschool model.

schools.name: Lights of Wonder Academy
schools.description: Lights of Wonder Academy is a faith-based microschool in Toronto serving students from first through eighth grade with diverse learning needs. The institution utilizes the Adaptive Multi-Sensory Unified Program, which prioritizes sensory regulation as the foundation for academic growth. This approach provides structured instruction within carefully designed sensory environments, aiming to support each child’s development through a combination of creative application and individualized attention in a family-centered setting.

founder.name: Sister Solana
founder.bio: Sister Solana D’Cunha, C.E., is the Foundress of Lights of Wonder Academy. With over sixteen years in exceptional student education, she previously served as a Special Education Teacher, Executive Functioning Strategies instructor, and program founder at Ave Maria Preparatory School.

schools.name: Our Village of Future Leaders Academy
schools.description: Our Village of Future Leaders Academy in Florence, South Carolina, serves students from kindergarten through sixth grade. Founded by an educator with over ten years of childcare experience, the microschool addresses concerns regarding declining literacy by utilizing an inquiry- and project-based curriculum. This approach emphasizes hands-on learning to strengthen academic understanding and confidence. The institution aims to build community while remaining accessible to families regardless of their ability to pay tuition.

founder.bio: Char founded Our Village of Future Leaders Academy, drawing on over ten years in childcare. As a single mother, she applies her educational passion to address declining academic skills while fostering community and holistic child development.

schools.name: Ranch & Roots Academy, LLC
schools.description: Ranch & Roots Academy is a private K-5 school located in San Juan County, New Mexico. The institution integrates core academic subjects with agricultural education through hands-on experiences such as gardening, livestock care, and farm-to-table nutrition. This model connects reading, writing, math, and science to practical life skills, emphasizing stewardship and character development within its faith-based curriculum for young learners.

founder.name: With
founder.bio: of Ranch & Roots Academy, LLC, she has 26 years of K–8 teaching experience. She holds a B.S. in Elementary Education, TESOL endorsement, and National Board Certification in Literacy for ages 3–12 as a Highly Qualified Level 3A instructional leader.

schools.name: Avant Christian Learning Center
schools.description: Avant Christian Learning Center, located in Sugar Grove, Pennsylvania, serves students from PreK through eighth grade. This hybrid institution integrates faith-based principles with its academic curriculum, offering flexible scheduling options to accommodate diverse family needs. The school positions itself as an alternative to traditional schooling by emphasizing the connection between religious values and educational content within a non-traditional learning environment.

founder.bio: of Avant Christian Learning Center, she holds a BS in Math Education and an MEd in Curriculum and Instruction. With six years of public school teaching experience, she established the microschool to provide an alternative educational option for her family and community.

schools.name: Kalexedy Learning Center
schools.description: Kalexedy Learning Center in Framingham, Massachusetts, serves students from third through twelfth grade. The school offers personalized academic programs designed to support individual growth at each student’s own pace. With a focus on developing essential skills and building confidence, the institution provides a structured environment where expert instructors help learners achieve their full potential both academically and socially within a small-group setting.

schools.name: The Dream Academy of CT
schools.description: The Dream Academy of Connecticut is a microschool located in New Haven, Connecticut, serving students in grades 3rd through 5th. Founded by Dr. Nordia Hewitt and TeQoa Griffith, the institution focuses on strengthening foundational skills in literacy, mathematics, and independent learning to prepare scholars for middle school. The program emphasizes personalized learning, family partnership, and holistic development to support academic, social, and emotional growth during these critical elementary years.

founder.name: Dr. Nordia
founder.bio: Dr. Nordia Hewitt founded The Dream Academy of CT. She is a literacy expert and multi-subject curriculum specialist with extensive experience leading K–12 academic initiatives in English Language Arts and humanities.

schools.name: E.L.L.A Learning Studio
schools.description: E.L.L.A Learning Studio operates in Houston, Texas, serving students in grades 9 through 12. This microschool offers a smaller educational setting designed to foster student confidence and independence. The curriculum emphasizes personalized, growth-driven instruction with a focus on accountability, aiming to provide a distinct pathway toward future academic and personal goals for its enrolled population.

founder.name: Jules Hampton
founder.bio: Jules Hampton founded E.L.L.A Learning Studio. He brings over a decade of experience across public, charter, private, and early college settings as a mathematics educator and instructional leader. Currently pursuing a doctorate in educational leadership, he applies research and innovative practices to the organization.

schools.name: EPIC Academy of Excellence
schools.description: EPIC Academy of Excellence is a virtual microschool in Powder Springs, Georgia, serving grades 6 through 12. Founded by educator Andrea Hall, it offers individualized instruction and project-based learning within small, mixed-age groups of five to ten students. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking and self-paced growth. Rooted in a faith-centered foundation, the school focuses on developing leadership, integrity, collaboration, and service alongside academic skills for its enrolled learners.

founder.name: Andrea Hall
founder.bio: Andrea Hall, M.Ed., founded EPIC Academy of Excellence. She holds degrees from Oakwood and Walden Universities and is a certified math educator. A former Teacher of the Year, she has over 15 years of online teaching experience.

schools.name: Morgan Preparatory Academy for Boys
schools.description: Morgan Preparatory Academy for Boys in McKinney, Texas, serves students in grades one through four. This therapeutic microschool tailors its curriculum to the developmental needs of young boys, emphasizing structured learning environments that integrate movement and hands-on activities. The program focuses on building emotional regulation, accountability, and character development alongside academic excellence, providing a specialized educational approach for this specific age group.

founder.name: Dr. Boykins
founder.bio: Dr. Boykins holds degrees in Biology, Special Education, and Behavior Analysis from UTC. As a district-level Behavior Analyst overseeing 40 special education personnel, she founded Morgan Preparatory Academy for Boys to support behavioral and academic growth through evidence-based practices.

schools.name: Live2Create Leadership Academy
schools.description: Live2Create Leadership Academy in Atlanta, Georgia, serves sixth through ninth graders in a small founding cohort launching Fall 2026. The school utilizes a studio-based model where students collaborate on real projects and build portfolios under the guidance of learning coaches and community mentors. Its distinct approach integrates faith as a central lens for exploring identity and purpose, focusing on leadership development rather than traditional classroom instruction.

founder.name: Amy P.
founder.bio: Amy P. McIntosh, a Senior Instructional Designer and nonprofit founder with 15 years of experience designing learning for adults, established Live2Create Leadership Academy to apply her expertise in intentional educational models to youth leadership development.

schools.name: Hundred Acre Learning Center
schools.description: Hundred Acre Learning Center is a faith-based microschool in Wayne, West Virginia, serving students from kindergarten through fifth grade. Founded by certified educator Wendy Collins, the school utilizes mixed-age groups of approximately twelve to fourteen children to foster a relationship-focused environment. The curriculum encourages exploration and play, aiming to support individual confidence and cultivate a lasting love for learning within a small community setting.

founder.name: Wendy Collins
founder.bio: Wendy Collins, a certified educator with over twenty years of experience at West Virginia Birth to Three and Logan County Schools, founded the faith-based Hundred Acre Learning Center in Wayne, West Virginia.

schools.name: The FOCUS Academy
schools.description: The FOCUS Academy in Memphis, Tennessee, is a microschool for sixth through eighth-grade boys who are twice-exceptional, meaning they are both gifted and neurodivergent. The program emphasizes flexible opportunities for creative and unique students to explore personal interests while developing strengths. It operates as a collaborative learning environment that combines the autonomy of homeschooling with the social dynamics of traditional peer groups.

founder.name: The
founder.bio: Karolyn Miller founded The FOCUS Academy. She is a nurse leader with 28 years of experience in private, public, and municipal school systems. As the parent of a twice-exceptional middle school boy, she advocates for equitable student support.

schools.name: Blossoming Imaginations
schools.description: Blossoming Imaginations is a microschool in Leesburg, Virginia, serving Kindergarten through 2nd grade. The program utilizes a nature-inspired, project-based curriculum that integrates hands-on exploration with academic instruction. Distinctive features include regular outdoor activities, art, and storytelling designed to support whole-child development. The school employs a small-group setting to provide individualized instruction tailored to each student’s specific strengths and learning style.

founder.name: Chavon Parker
founder.bio: Chavon Parker owns Blossoming Imaginations. A former teacher with dyslexia and a background in graphic communications and animation, she previously taught Pre-K and kindergarten in private school settings, leveraging her experience to support diverse learning needs.

schools.name: ME Institute
schools.description: The ME Institute in Memphis, Tennessee, serves students from Kindergarten through 7th Grade. This microschool offers career-driven, student-centered programs that emphasize real-world learning experiences. The institution provides personalized instruction tailored to individual strengths and needs. Additionally, the curriculum integrates faith-based teachings to explore the connection between faith, culture, and human development, aiming to help students discover their purpose and navigate life with confidence.

founder.name: La
founder.bio: LaSonya Woods founded ME Institute. With over 25 years in public education and roles as an executive director, she specializes in instructional leadership, individualized education planning, and student advocacy for non-traditional learners.

schools.name: Dream Builders Learning Center
schools.description: Dream Builders Learning Center serves grades K through 5th in Nashville, Tennessee. This microschool utilizes a whole-child approach to provide academic support and social-emotional well-being within an affirming environment. The curriculum features project-based learning opportunities including computer science with AI and VR, as well as entrepreneurship and financial literacy. The program aims to build student confidence, strengthen critical thinking skills, and promote social justice.

founder.name: My
founder.bio: Micaela Watson holds a master’s in education from UCLA and a bachelor’s in psychology from the College of Wooster. She founded Dream Builders Learning Center after three years at Vanderbilt University conducting literacy intervention, classroom observations, and student assessments.

schools.name: Willow Oaks Micro School
schools.description: Willow Oaks Micro School in Garland, Texas, serves students from Kindergarten through second grade. The program supports children transitioning from childcare or home environments by utilizing a hybrid delivery model that blends traditional and non-traditional teaching methods. It emphasizes movement-based learning, smaller class sizes, and individualized attention to accommodate highly active or sensory-seeking learners while fostering confidence and self-paced achievement.

founder.name: In
founder.bio: Jane Doe founded Willow Oaks Micro School to support neurodivergent learners. With a background in special education, she established a small, structured environment that welcomes movement and encourages curiosity for children experiencing the world with extra energy.

schools.name: Kingdom Scholars Microschool
schools.description: Kingdom Scholars Microschool serves students in grades K through 5th Grade in Xenia, Ohio. The institution offers a Christ-centered educational environment designed for smaller class sizes and personalized instruction. Its curriculum emphasizes strong academics alongside character development, life skills, and faith-based values. The school prioritizes close family partnerships and hands-on learning experiences to support individual student growth within a nurturing community setting.

founder.name: Rhonda Porter
founder.bio: Rhonda Porter, founder of Kingdom Scholars Microschool, holds a master’s degree in Special Education from the American College of Education. With over 13 years of experience supporting diverse learning styles, she established the school to provide intentional, faith-centered education.

schools.name: Hope Christian Academy
schools.description: Hope Christian Academy operates as a faith-based microschool in Paris, Illinois, serving students in third through eighth grades. The program utilizes a project-driven curriculum led by certified teachers to provide an alternative to traditional public schooling. Rooted in a biblical worldview, the school emphasizes individual purpose and accommodates diverse abilities. Located in a community with limited private options, it offers a distinct educational path for local families seeking hands-on learning experiences.

founder.name: God
founder.bio: of Hope Christian Academy, she is a mother of three and a teacher with 20 years of experience. She established the school after observing her son struggle in public education, aiming to provide alternative options for students who do not fit that system.

schools.name: Identity Preparatory Academy
schools.description: Identity Preparatory Academy in Omaha serves girls in grades four through eight. The microschool focuses on learner identity, purpose, and leadership within a supportive environment. Its curriculum and educator selection emphasize representation of the student population and community history. This approach aims to equip students with specific skills and confidence for academic success and personal development.

founder.name: Dr.
founder.bio: Dr. DérNecia Phillips, an adjunct instructor at the University of Nebraska at Omaha and former principal, founded Identity Preparatory Academy in North Omaha to serve as a middle school for girls.

schools.name: Aristotle’s Garden Micro-Academy
schools.description: Aristotle’s Garden Micro-Academy in San Antonio, Texas, serves fourth through sixth graders through a mastery-based curriculum grounded in Socratic philosophy. The program emphasizes deep reading, writing, and discussion within small groups of up to twelve students. This structure prioritizes intellectual depth over rapid pacing, offering a specialized environment for learners who may require additional support or distinct pedagogical approaches compared to traditional schooling models.

founder.bio: of Aristotle’s Garden Micro-Academy is an experienced educator with over seven years teaching middle school in Texas public schools. She specializes in supporting students with ADHD, autism, and diverse learning needs through a Socratic, mastery-based approach.

schools.name: PGF Learning Academy
schools.description: PGF Learning Academy is a microschool launching in Montgomery, Alabama, in August 2026 for students in grades three through seven. Serving a cohort of twelve scholars aged nine to fourteen, the institution focuses on addressing foundational academic gaps in reading and core subjects. The program utilizes personalized, mastery-based instruction designed to support student development within a small-group educational setting.

founder.name: Mrs. Mottenon
founder.bio: Mrs. Mottenon founded PGF Learning Academy after 22 years in education, including 12 years teaching and 10 years as a Parent Involvement Facilitator. She holds a Life Sciences degree from Indiana State University, a Master’s in Family Therapy, and certifications from Marian and Troy Universities.

schools.name: Marvelous Treasures Academy, LLC
schools.description: Marvelous Treasures Academy, LLC serves PreK through 12th-grade students in Houston, Texas. This microschool specifically supports learners with ADHD and executive functioning challenges by combining academics with explicit instruction in organization, time management, planning, and self-regulation. The program emphasizes social and emotional growth within a structured environment designed to help students develop confidence and essential life skills.

founder.name: The
founder.bio: The founder of Marvelous Treasures Academy previously served as a supervisor in customer service for ten years. She then spent thirty years in education as a special education teacher, counselor, behavior specialist, and coordinator, followed by founding Marvelous Counseling & Therapy in 2015.

schools.name: Micro School Powered by Huntington Learning Center
schools.description: Micro School Powered by Huntington Learning Center serves students in Mansfield, Texas, from kindergarten through eighth grade. founder.name: In
founder.bio: Anne Huntington Sharma serves as President and CEO of the microschool powered by Huntington Learning Center. She leads the organization co-founded in 1977 by her parents, Eileen Huntington, a former high school teacher, and Dr. Raymond Huntington, a former college professor and senior business analyst.

schools.name: Empowerment Leadership Academy
schools.description: Empowerment Leadership Academy is a microschool in Atascocita, Texas, serving grades six through twelve. It specializes in supporting gifted but inconsistent learners, including those with executive functioning challenges like ADHD. The program integrates rigorous academics with intentional leadership training and character development. Students receive personalized support to build accountability, communication skills, and self-discipline within a structured environment designed to foster critical thinking and personal growth alongside academic achievement.

founder.name: Dr. Ulelia
founder.bio: Dr. Ulelia Childs founded Empowerment Leadership Academy. An educator and instructional leader with over 15 years of experience, she previously served as an English teacher, assistant principal, and principal while supervising campus principals.

schools.name: Elite Flexi School
schools.description: Elite Flexi School in Austin, Texas, serves students from first through twelfth grade. The institution primarily focuses on grades six through twelve but also accommodates younger children to allow families to keep all their offspring in one location. The school offers a Christian-based educational environment that integrates faith and values into its curriculum, aiming to align with the religious principles of its community while providing flexible learning options tailored to individual student goals.

founder.name: Proudly
founder.bio: of Elite Flexi School, he brings 27 years of experience in private schools, distance education, and microschools. He remains a director and shareholder in a private school with 450 students, focusing on specialized training for aspiring pilots, athletes, and professionals.

schools.name: Explora
schools.description: Explora is a part-time microschool in Saint Cloud, Florida, serving grades K through 5. The program emphasizes interdisciplinary learning with low-tech instruction hours to cultivate critical thinking and adaptability. Core curriculum features structured math and language arts alongside natural Spanish immersion. Students engage in financial literacy application, entrepreneurship projects, and Socratic discussions. Physical movement and creative arts are integrated as essential components of the educational experience rather than optional add-ons.

founder.name: As
founder.bio: of Explora holds a Master’s degree in bilingual education and mathematics. Her background includes K-12 teaching, curriculum design, and leading STEM clubs, art programs, and camps. She established the microschool to foster intellectually curious and emotionally aware children through a human-centered educational approach.

schools.name: Unity Sanctuary
schools.description: Unity Sanctuary in Austin, Texas, serves students from PreK through 12th grade within a multi-generational campus model. The facility integrates academic instruction with dedicated co-working spaces for guardians, wellness areas, and community zones. This design facilitates simultaneous learning for children and professional or personal development for parents, fostering an environment that prioritizes family involvement and holistic well-being over traditional drop-off structures.

founder.name: For
founder.bio: Unity Sanctuary founder previously worked in real estate before dedicating eighteen months to reflection and prayer. She transitioned into early childhood education after recognizing her own emotional intensity within preschool classrooms, aiming to help children rather than control them.

schools.name: Innovations Leadership Academy
schools.description: Located in Fort Worth, Texas, Innovations Leadership Academy serves students from kindergarten through eighth grade. The school utilizes a blended-learning model that combines online digital media with traditional classroom methods. Its distinct approach centers on personalized competency-based education and project-based learning. This framework aims to address individual student needs while fostering social-emotional aptitude, career readiness, and access to technology within a rigorous academic environment.

founder.name: Markus Baskerville
founder.bio: Markus Baskerville founded Innovations Leadership Academy. He previously served as a charter school campus principal in Dallas/Ft. Worth, focusing on strategic planning, teacher development, and standards-based curriculum implementation.

schools.name: Keystone Potential Studio
schools.description: Keystone Potential Studio serves third through fifth graders in Cincinnati, Ohio. The microschool utilizes a mastery-based curriculum that allows students to progress at their own pace. Instruction combines personalized academic guidance with independent study and hands-on creative projects. The program emphasizes social-emotional development and real-world application, fostering student ownership of learning. This approach aims to build confidence and support individualized growth within a flexible educational framework.

founder.name: Dena Combs
founder.bio: Dena Combs founded Keystone Potential Studio. She brings over ten years of experience as an educator, math coach, and Assistant Principal of Instruction to the microschool.

schools.name: Harbor Village Academy
schools.description: Harbor Village Academy is an autism-focused microschool located in Denton County, Texas, serving students from Pre-K through fifth grade. The institution provides individualized, evidence-based education tailored to learners with autism and related learning differences. Its distinct approach emphasizes language-rich instruction and integrated support across academic, social, emotional, and developmental domains to foster communication skills and independence while maintaining active family partnership in the educational process.

founder.name: Dr. Leanna
founder.bio: Dr. Leanna Hodges founded Harbor Village Academy. She is a special educator and mother who utilizes evidence-based practices to support students with autism. Her background includes differentiated instruction and language-rich teaching to foster academic growth and independence.

schools.name: Calmecac In Lak'Ech
schools.description: Located in San Antonio, Texas, Calmecac In Lak'Ech serves students in grades five through twelve. The school distinguishes itself by integrating Indigenous knowledge with S.T.E.A.M education to support social-emotional learning and holistic wellbeing. Its curriculum emphasizes land-based learning and intergenerational instruction, aiming to foster cultural identity preservation while developing critical thinking and community well-being among its student body.

founder.name: Laura Yohualtlahuiz
founder.bio: Laura Yohualtlahuiz Rios-Ramirez founded Calmecac In Lak'Ech. A 2-spirit Xicana scholar with Tepehuan and Guachichil heritage, they bring nearly 30 years of experience as an educator and researcher in San Antonio, Texas, specializing in indigenous healing justice and pedagogical strategy.

schools.name: The Academy
schools.description: The Academy is a microschool in Hernando, Mississippi, serving students in grades 6 through 10. The program combines multi-age community time with small-group instruction in core subjects, allowing for personalized academic pacing. Students engage in collaborative exploration of interest-based topics, emphasizing emotional intelligence and resilience. This model supports adolescents seeking structured environments that prioritize both personal development and academic achievement within a cohesive, supportive framework.

founder.name: Dr. Ny
founder.bio: Dr. Ny G. is a former U.S. Army Officer and JAG Corps acceptee with a doctoral degree in law and policy. A Portland native raised in a military family, she founded The Academy after relocating to Mississippi in 2015 to support her daughter’s learning needs.

schools.name: Suenos STEAM School
schools.description: Suenos STEAM School is an alternative high school in Las Cruces, New Mexico, serving grades 9 through 12. It integrates academic instruction with structured recovery support for students managing trauma, PTSD, or substance use challenges. The school utilizes the Amethyst framework to combine rehabilitative systems with educational pedagogy. Its distinct model features a trauma-informed environment offering counseling and recovery programming alongside personalized learning plans and STEAM-based project work.

founder.name: Mack Neal
founder.bio: Mack Neal holds multiple master’s degrees and is a licensed educational administrator. As the founder of Amethyst Youth Recovery and Learning Center and Suenos STEAM School, he integrates technical innovation with modernized 12-step recovery models.

schools.name: Wind Rose Academy
schools.description: Wind Rose Academy is a microschool in Plano, Texas, serving grades PreK through 12th Grade. It provides individualized therapeutic services and education specifically for students on the autism spectrum. The school distinguishes itself by integrating innovative Applied Behavior Analysis therapy with adaptive small-group classes and engaging extracurricular activities to support student independence and address specific adaptive needs.

founder.name: Jennifer Keese
founder.bio: Jennifer Keese is the founder of Wind Rose Academy and Clinical Director for Concept Connections. A BCBA, special educator, and certified Autism Interventionist with over 20 years of experience, she has received recognition from DFW Magazine and Dominique Cares Non Profit.

schools.name: The Kingdom School of Excellence
schools.description: The Kingdom School of Excellence is a full-time microschool in Duluth, Georgia, serving students in grades two through five. The program offers personalized academic pathways allowing learners to master core subjects at their own pace within a mixed-age environment. Daily activities include Scripture-based goal setting and participation in an Innovation Lab where students develop entrepreneurship skills by transforming creative ideas into real-world business concepts.

founder.name: For
founder.bio: of The Kingdom School of Excellence, this educator holds a Bachelor’s in Early Childhood and Special Education and a Master’s in Urban Teacher Leadership from Georgia State University. With 17 years as a teacher in metro Atlanta, she focuses on personalized academic pathways for students with learning differences.

schools.name: Root and Bloom Academy
schools.description: Root and Bloom Academy serves PreK through 3rd-grade students in McAllen, Texas, offering a Montessori-inspired microschool model. The program emphasizes personalized, holistic education within small class sizes to accommodate individual learning needs. Instructional approaches utilize gentle parenting principles rather than traditional reward systems to foster student empathy and resilience. This distinct methodology aims to cultivate creativity and independent problem-solving skills in a supportive academic environment.

founder.name: Sunaina Chugani
founder.bio: Sunaina Chugani Marquez spent 18 years researching consumer psychology at Baruch College, San Diego State University, and UTRGV before co-founding Root and Bloom Academy with her husband, Matt Marquez.

schools.name: Tiny Oaks Montessori
schools.description: Tiny Oaks Montessori is a microschool in Merritt Island, Florida, serving students from Pre-K through third grade. The program utilizes the Montessori method within a prepared environment to support intellectual, social, and emotional development. Educators act as guides, balancing structure with freedom to encourage self-directed activity and independence. This approach emphasizes hands-on learning and community connection, fostering respect and inclusion for the whole child.

founder.name: Adina Box
founder.bio: Adina Box founded Tiny Oaks Montessori. With over 20 years in early childhood education and 12 years as a fitness instructor, she brings extensive experience in program leadership, teacher mentoring, and creating holistic learning environments for children and families.

schools.name: Claypool Creek
schools.description: Claypool Creek serves students in grades K through 12th Grade within Deltona, Florida. Founded by Headmistress Megan Hampton, the microschool offers a bespoke curriculum designed to bridge high-level logical reasoning with personalized instruction. The institution emphasizes architectural rigor alongside intentional hospitality, aiming to foster academic excellence through a customized educational approach tailored to individual student needs.

founder.name: For
